page.layout: One printed page (p. 134) with running head at top, text block in one column, a woodcut ornament below the text, and a catchword at the lower right. At the right edge of the scan is a narrow strip of the facing page (p. 135) with a cut-off running text and marginal notes. That strip is the edge of the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.
page.running_head: LIB. I. CAP. XIII. / Juris humani origo

main_text.p: nibus deductæ, proque locorum, temporum ac personarum ratione specificationes atque determinationes à magistratu additę illis sunt. Nec pro lege habenda est, quæ diversum à jure naturæ, aut Decalogo repugnans statuit. Qualis fuit illa lex Spartana, quæ pacisci cum alterius conjuge, aut prostituere cōjuges & filias ex pacto concedebat. Ac quid legibus Romanis majus aut præclarius tribui potest, quàm cùm prima earum delineatio & adumbratio in sapientiæ divinæ vestigiis demonstratur, illarumq; architectus & vindex Deus constituitur? Quòd si verò universi juris doctrina ex Decalogo exstructa est; ex eodem autem Decalogo forenses etiam leges Mosaicas, quæ quidem universales, immutabiles & perpetuæ sunt, petitas demonstrari queat; quis sanus his refragabitur?

page.notes: The woodcut ornament below the text is a decorative tailpiece with a central mask and foliage; it is not text and is not transcribed. The strip of the facing page at the right edge is cropped and not legible enough to transcribe. The running head's left part is printed as "LIB.I.CAP.XIII." and is given with spacing as "LIB. I. CAP. XIII." The word "LIBRI" at lower right is printed in spaced capitals and is treated as the catchword.
